parts.text: In this experiment, you will investigate the resistance of a wire. Carry out the following instructions, referring to Fig. 3.1. Fig. 3.1

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) Close the switch. Measure the current I in the circuit. I = ......................................................... [1]

ms.label: 3(a)
ms.text: I to at least 2 decimal places and < 1 A

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) Place the sliding contact at a distance l = 5.0 cm from B . Measure, and record in Table 3.1, the potential difference (p.d.) V across the length l of resistance wire BC . Open the switch. Calculate, and record in Table 3.1, the resistance R of 5.0 cm of the resistance wire using the equation R = V I . Close the switch. Repeat the procedure in (b) using l values of 25.0 cm, 45.0 cm, 65.0 cm and 85.0 cm. Open the switch. Table 3.1 l / cm V / V R / Ω 5.0 25.0 45.0 65.0 85.0 [4]

ms.label: 3(b)
ms.text:
all V values to at least 1 decimal place and < 3 V
V values increasing
R values correct
R values to consistent 2 or consistent 3 significant figures

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) Plot a graph of R / Ω ( y -axis) against l / cm ( x -axis). Start both axes at the origin (0,0). 0 0 [4]

ms.label: 3(c)

graph:

suitable scales

parts.label: d
parts.text: (d) Use your graph to determine the resistance R 50 of 50.0 cm of the resistance wire. Show clearly on the graph how you obtained the necessary information. R 50 = ........................................................... Ω [2]
